points.why: It says to put numbers on it now as ranges, and argues that writing down the leads' unstated numbers will settle a deadlock that debate won't.
It notes each lead likely holds a different unstated number, but never has each lead write their own equations and compare them before running.
It gives a strong sensitivity test and collects data only on the parameters the decision flips on, but never steps the model forward by hand.
It has no guard against anchoring: no independent estimates and no warning against the first-draft guess becoming the default.

pitfalls.why: It explicitly rejects waiting and quantifies now with ranges.

notes: The answer supplies its own default ranges (5–30% deflection, 2–4 month ramp), which risks anchoring both leads on those numbers.
